title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཛེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 188)
shelf_note: A Derge woodblock folio of a pramāṇa commentary (valid cognition, arthakriyā, svalakṣaṇa, 'rtog pa sngon du gtong ba'). It belongs in the Tshad ma section of the Tengyur.

ocr_errors.image: the initial glyph looks like ཇི (ཇི་ལྟར)
ocr_errors.problem: possible ཅི/ཇི confusion. It does not change the meaning; low confidence at this resolution

ocr_errors.image: line 7 seems to have one or two more syllables after དངོས་པོ than the OCR (maybe འགའ་ཞིག), but I cannot read them clearly

tr_errors_A.english: Whatever analytical inquiry examines valid cognition and related topics possesses an object suitable...
tr_errors_A.problem: The source means 'any investigation, such as valid cognition'. A makes valid cognition the topic being examined, which does not fit A's own later 'valid cognition or other forms of investigation'

tr_errors_A.english: a thinker would not investigate things through cognition, because cognition itself is not what directly performs...
tr_errors_A.problem: 'cognition endowed with conceptuality' is split into 'a thinker' plus plain 'cognition', so the objection loses its point, which is about CONCEPTUAL cognition

tr_errors_A.english: non-deceptive because it reveals the specifically characterized phenomenon
tr_errors_A.problem: 'object of engagement' (འཇུག་པའི་ཡུལ) is dropped from the main text; it survives only in the gloss
the keyword names the text without support; nothing on the page identifies it

tr_errors_B.english: Whatever investigation of valid cognition occurs
tr_errors_B.problem: The source means 'investigation such as valid cognition'; B renders it as an investigation OF valid cognition

tr_errors_B.english: we do not observe that the mere desire for an object like fire constitutes the goal of a seeker of causal efficacy
tr_errors_B.problem: The source says fire etc. is not seen to be obtained merely by wanting it. B says instead that the desire is not the goal

tr_errors_B.english: then conceptual cognition should not be investigated
tr_errors_B.problem: conceptual cognition is the INSTRUMENT of investigation (instrumental ས), but B makes it the object being investigated

tr_errors_B.english: how both factors become branches of causal efficacy through a single engagement, the text mentions "preceded by conceptualization."
tr_errors_B.problem: The source says the one expression shows both points. B turns this into 'both factors become branches through a single engagement', which garbles why the root text says 'preceded by conceptualization'

tr_errors_B.english: It is the capacity for causal efficacy
tr_errors_B.problem: the page opens mid-sentence ('…is capable of'). B turns the fragment into a free-standing claim and does not mark the continuation
an attribution that nothing on the page supports (it is hedged)

pages.prefer_reason: Neither version has a serious error, but B has four moderate misreadings (the fire sentence, conceptual cognition as object instead of instrument, the 'single expression' reply, the opening clause) where A has two.

book_verdict: This is a clean Derge pramāṇa folio and the transcription is close to the block print. Both English versions are serviceable, with no reversals. A is the more faithful, but both misconstrue 'ཚད་མ་ལ་སོགས་པ་དཔྱོད་པ' and the conceptual-cognition objection.
